claims.text: An AWD-LSTM is trained on a large, general corpus to capture universal language features.
claims.reason: Paper explicitly states 'we use the state-of-the-art language model AWD-LSTM' pretrained on Wikitext-103 for general-domain LM pretraining.

claims.text: Training involves Adam optimization with β1 = 0.7.
claims.reason: Paper states 'We use Adam with β1 = 0.7 instead of the default β1 = 0.9' in the hyperparameters section.

claims.text: Discriminative fine-tuning assigns different learning rates to different layers with η_{l-1} = η_l / 2.
claims.reason: Paper specifies the divisor as 2.6, not 2: 'η^{l-1} = η^l / 2.6 as the learning rate for lower layers'.

claims.text: General-domain pretraining was conducted on Wikitext-103, consisting of 103 million words from 28,595 Wikipedia articles.
claims.reason: Paper states exactly 'Wikitext-103 (Merity et al., 2017b) consisting of 28,595 preprocessed Wikipedia articles and 103 million words'.

claims.text: The method was evaluated on six representative text classification datasets across three tasks: sentiment analysis (IMDb, Yelp binary and five-class), question classification (TREC-6), and topic classification (AG News and DBpedia).
claims.reason: Paper confirms all six datasets across three tasks in Table 1 and Section 4.1.

claims.text: IMDb has 25k examples and is a binary classification dataset.
claims.reason: Table 1 in the paper lists IMDb as Sentiment type with 2 classes and 25k examples.

claims.text: TREC-6 has 5.5k examples and six classes.
claims.reason: Table 1 confirms TREC-6 has 6 classes and 5.5k training examples.

claims.text: AG News has 120k examples and four classes.
claims.reason: Table 1 confirms AG has 4 classes and 120k training examples.
Table 1 confirms DBpedia has 14 classes and 560k training examples.

claims.text: ULMFiT significantly outperforms state-of-the-art baselines, reducing error by 18-24% on most datasets.
claims.reason: Paper abstract and contributions section state 'reducing the error by 18-24% on the majority of datasets'.

claims.text: With only 100 labels, ULMFiT can match the performance of models trained from scratch with 10 to 100 times more data.
claims.reason: Paper states with 100 labeled examples ULMFiT matches training from scratch with 10x more data (supervised on IMDb) and up to 100x more data (semi-supervised on AG), per Section 5 and the abstract.

claims.text: ULMFiT was compared against DPCNN and oh-LSTM as state-of-the-art models.
claims.reason: Table 2 explicitly names 'IMDb oh-LSTM (Johnson and Zhang, 2016)' and Table 3 includes 'DPCNN (Johnson and Zhang, 2017)' as comparison baselines.
